tagline: Thailand's northernmost city, with striking temples, high mountains, and tea farms
introHtml: Chiang Rai is Thailand's northernmost province, a city you can wander slowly all day without getting bored. It has temples designed by local artists, mountains and tea farms where you can sit and sip coffee in the cool air, and the Golden Triangle, where you can stand in one spot and watch the Mekong River run past three countries. If you like a calm pace and cool weather, this place hits the mark.
bestTime: November–February, cool and clear with flowers in bloom

highlights.name: Wat Rong Khun (White Temple)
highlights.blurb: Ajarn Chalermchai Kositpipat's all-white temple, covered in finely detailed stucco work. It's become the image people picture when they think of Chiang Rai.

highlights.name: Doi Tung
highlights.blurb: The Doi Tung Royal Villa and Mae Fah Luang Garden, where flowers bloom beautifully year-round and the air stays cool and pleasant.

highlights.name: Golden Triangle
highlights.blurb: The point where the Mekong River divides Thailand, Laos, and Myanmar. Stand in one place and look out over three countries.

highlights.name: Doi Chang tea farms
highlights.blurb: Coffee country and terraced tea farms. Head up and sip a drink in the middle of green fields all day.

highlights.name: Wat Rong Suea Ten (Blue Temple)
highlights.blurb: A deep-blue hall trimmed in gold, with contemporary Buddhist sculpture that photographs well from every angle.

highlights.name: Phu Chi Fa
highlights.blurb: A favorite sea-of-fog viewpoint for nature lovers. Wake up early to watch the sunrise over the valley.

foodScene.name: Northern Thai food
foodScene.note: Khao soi, nam ngiao, and gaeng hang lay are easy to find around town, full-flavored the way northerners like it.

foodScene.name: Sai ua and khaep mu
foodScene.note: The local sausage and pork crackling, both a popular souvenir and a side dish. Snack on them or eat with sticky rice.

foodScene.name: Beef noodles
foodScene.note: Several old shops in town serve a rich broth with tender beef. Locals eat it regularly.

foodScene.name: Mountain coffee cafes
foodScene.note: Chiang Rai grows its own coffee at Doi Chang and Doi Tung, and cafes with tea-farm views are everywhere.

foodScene.name: Akha hill-tribe food
foodScene.note: Local dishes from the hill-tribe communities up in the mountains, with unfamiliar flavors worth trying, found around the hilltop villages.

foodScene.name: Kad Luang Market
foodScene.note: The fresh market in the center of town, with local food, sweets, and mountain vegetables to graze on in the morning.

foodScene.name: Chiang Rai Walking Street
foodScene.note: Open Saturday and Sunday, gathering northern street food, traditional sweets, and grilled snacks to eat as you stroll.

attractions.name: Wat Rong Khun (White Temple)
attractions.blurb: The white temple that has become Chiang Rai's symbol, with every square inch of art designed by Ajarn Chalermchai.

attractions.name: Wat Rong Suea Ten (Blue Temple)
attractions.blurb: A deep-blue hall where the contemporary sculpture and murals catch the eye.

attractions.name: Mae Fah Luang Garden, Doi Tung
attractions.blurb: A beautifully designed flower garden on the mountain with a royal villa to walk through, cool air all year.

attractions.name: Phu Chi Fa
attractions.blurb: A spot for the sea of fog and sunrise, good for early risers and nature lovers.

attractions.name: Golden Triangle
attractions.blurb: On the bank of the Mekong where you can see the borders of three countries, with an opium museum to visit.

attractions.name: Commemorative Clock Tower
attractions.blurb: The downtown landmark designed by Ajarn Chalermchai, with a color-changing light show after dark.

attractions.name: Choui Fong Tea Plantation
attractions.blurb: Terraced tea fields green as far as the eye can see, with a cafe to sit and sip tea over the rolling hills.

attractions.name: Wat Huay Pla Kang
attractions.blurb: A nine-tier Chinese-style pagoda on a hill. Climb up to pay respects and take in a wide view of the city.
